main_issue: Whether the housewarming should serve alcohol (A's purchased drinks) given D's religious objection, or use a compromise like a cooler box or alcohol-free party

A-B.evidence: B offers cooler solutions (8, 23) and says 'We're all hosts' (15) against A's 'don't be a host'; A never adopts the compromises and still insists on alcohol (26).

A-C.evidence: C backs the cooler ideas and says the dispute must be resolved (9, 18, 24); A keeps pushing back and says 'three of us live here too' (26), counting C on A's side though C never takes it up.

A-D.evidence: D rejects alcohol at the party and offers an alcohol-free party and repayment (19, 21); A refuses: 'It's either your way, or nothing' (26).

B-C.evidence: C endorses B's cooler box (9) and the landing cooler (24), and agrees on needing to resolve it (18).

B-D.evidence: B defends D as a host (15) but D rejects B's cooler proposals (11, 25), so they agree on D's inclusion but not the arrangement.

C-D.evidence: C supports cooler options (9, 24) that D declines (11, 25); C takes no stand on the alcohol-free idea.
